basis: per month per $1,000 of the outstanding insured indebtedness
rate_table_note: Rates are in paragraph 2 of the rule. A single premium is the summation of the monthly premiums at $1.23 (2(b)); joint credit life on the debtor and one co-signer is at most 150% of these rates (2(d)). Neither is published as a figure, so neither is recorded.
summary: Rates in force: Alabama's maximum credit life rates in Banking rule 155-2-2-.12 as amended June 1, 2018: $1.23 per month per $1,000 of outstanding insured indebtedness, and $1.60 per $100 per annum on single payment contracts. Insurance rule 482-1-117-.10 makes the maximum rates of the Superintendent of Banks the prima facie rates for consumer loans and sales. June 1, 2018 is the rule's last amendment; whether it changed these figures was not confirmed from an official copy of the earlier text.

basis: single premium per $100 of initial indebtedness (total of payments)
rate_table_note: Rates are from the table in paragraph 3 of the rule ("Rate Per $100 of Initial Indebtedness"), rows for indebtedness payable in 12 and 60 months; the table runs from 1 to 120 months plus $.20 for each additional 12 months, and other terms are interpolated. "Initial indebtedness" means the total of payments. The column headings print as "Non-Retroacive" [sic] Benefits (14-day, 30-day) and Retroactive Benefits (7-day, 14-day, 30-day); the text extraction runs the heading lines together, so the columns were read from their positions on the page. Joint coverage is at most 185% of these rates (paragraph 6). Higher rates need a deviation approved by the Banking and Insurance Departments (paragraph 4; 482-1-117-.18).

June 1, 2018 is the rule's last amendment; whether it changed these figures was not confirmed from an official copy of the earlier text.

source_title: Ala. Admin. Code ch. 482-1-093, Credit Property and Involuntary Unemployment Insurance, Exhibit B (Department of Insurance; revised July 23, 2002, effective August 2, 2002)
plan: Monthly outstanding balance (Table 1), 12-month benefit period, 30-day elimination and 30-day waiting period, non-retroactive
rate_table_note: Rates are from Exhibit B, Tables 1 to 3, rows for a 12-month benefit period (each table also gives 3, 6 and 9 months). Table 1 assumes a monthly indemnity of 3% of the monthly outstanding balance and is adjusted proportionally otherwise. A single premium is the number of months in the loan term times the Table 3 rate. The rates assume single coverage for involuntary layoff, termination, strikes, labor disputes and lockouts. Joint IUI sold under the Consumer Credit Act is at most 175% of single (Banking rule 155-2-2-.12, paragraph 7).
summary: Rates in force: Alabama's presumptive IUI rates in Exhibit B of Department of Insurance chapter 482-1-093 (rule 482-1-093-.10(b): rates not above Exhibit B are presumed reasonable; higher rates need a loss ratio of at least 50%). The chapter was revised July 23, 2002, effective August 2, 2002, and the revisions apply to policies sold after December 31, 2002, so January 1, 2003 is used. No later revision is listed on the Department's regulations page.
